title: Priority Scoring Engine for Org-level Identity Requests (SSO / SCIM / RBAC)
creator: Arianna Chen
description: Design and deliver an automated priority-scoring engine that classifies and ranks incoming org-level identity requests (SSO/SAML enablement, SCIM provisioning, tenant RBAC changes) so that support, success, and product ops can route and fulfill requests with predictable SLAs. This ticket covers the PM scope: scoring rubric, integration contract for intake UI, fallback manual overrides, and rollout plan with metrics for effectiveness.
background: Enterprise customers have been asking for faster, more consistent outcomes for access-related requests. Current intake is manual and inconsistent: similar requests are handled in different queues and SLA variance is high. We need a deterministic scoring model that combines risk, customer tier, expected engineering effort, and compliance sensitivity to surface priority and required approval paths.
proposed_solution: 1) Define a lightweight, auditable scoring rubric with weighted signals: customer_tier, grant_scope (org vs team), complexity_estimate, data_sensitivity, compliance_flags (e.g., GDPR/HIPAA), and requested_by_role. 2) Implement a service (intake-priority) that returns a score (0-100) and suggested route (support, success, security review, engineering). 3) Integrate the score into the existing intake UI (Console) and add a manual override for admins with justification. 4) Emit events to observability pipeline for calibration and regression detection.
acceptance_criteria: A rubric document exists with normalized weights and examples for common request types
API endpoint /intake/score returns consistent score and route for seeded sample payloads
Console ingest flow surfaces score and suggested route, and allows override with justification
Automated metrics dashboard shows distribution of scores and correlation with fulfillment time
SLA routing rules in the queueing system honor score thresholds and trigger escalation policies
implementation_notes: Start with a rules-based model to get early predictability; keep schema small and extensible. Instrument every decision with traceable fields for audits. Work with Security to ensure compliance flags are exhaustive. Plan a later phase to evaluate ML-based ranking using historical intake and fulfillment data.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (pilot): ship rules-based scorer for top 20% of incoming enterprise org requests and route to a 'priority' queue for two customers in the beta cohort. Phase 2 (widen): expand to all enterprise customers and add dashboarding. Phase 3 (iterate): incorporate heuristic tuning and optional ML ranking; enable automated escalations.
metrics: Time-to-first-action by score bucket, percentage of overrides, accuracy of suggested route (match to final owner), mean time-to-resolution for top quartile, false positives (unnecessary escalations)
stakeholders: PM: Arianna Chen; Eng owner: Diego Morales; Security: Priya Nair; Support lead: Elena Ruiz; Success lead: Marcus Bell
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: overly aggressive scoring leads to unnecessary engineering escalations. Mitigation: conservative initial thresholds and pilot with manual review. Risk: missed compliance flags. Mitigation: require security sign-off on rubric and include mandatory check for flagged requests.
